objective: Proof: a counting law whose triangle rule is the graph of a partial operation on a finite label set satisfies the ordered 2-3 and 1-4 identities with positive constants exactly when the triangles lying in allowed tetrahedra are the composable triples of a finite groupoid whose components all have the same number of objects times vertex-group order; triangles in no allowed tetrahedron never enter an identity; lambda = 1, mu is that common value, and the normalized count on a closed connected three-manifold is the sum over components of |Hom(pi1(M), G_i)|/|G_i|. Standard-library checks: every partial operation on at most three labels, groupoids with up to eight arrows, merged-label and non-group controls, and the count formula on sampled ordered triangulations.
status: Proved by PATTERN-3D-20261025-001A-P001: a counting law whose long edge is a function of the two short edges survives the ordered 2-3 and 1-4 moves exactly when its triangles lying in allowed tetrahedra are the compositions of a finite groupoid whose components share the value objects times group order (lambda = 1, mu that value); triangles in no allowed tetrahedron never matter; the objects are the idempotent labels, recovered because the units of different blocks always form an allowed tetrahedron. The invariant is the sum of |Hom(pi1(M), G_i)|/|G_i|, so deterministic counting sees only homomorphisms into finite groups: lens spaces of equal order and the pairs of Funar and Hempel are never separated.
title: The moves force a groupoid
